text:
alex: Heads-up: support flagged a customer seeing apparent double token charges when a streaming session reconnects and a toolcall gets truncated mid-retry. Anyone looked into resume + truncation interactions recently?

sam: Not yet. Do we have a repro or request ids? Could be similar to past route-handoff cases but truncation may change final ack semantics.

alex: Repro request id: req_20260302_99. Minimal log excerpt (sanitized): ```{\n  \"session\": \"sess_X\",\n  \"req\": \"req_20260302_99\",\n  \"provisional_tokens\": 90,\n  \"resume_route\": \"us-west-2-b\",\n  \"toolcall_truncated\": true,\n  \"confirmed_tokens\": 210\n}```

maria: That looks like provisional wasn't cleared before the resumed host confirmed the new token count. We should tag ledger events with origin route and resume session id to join them.

danny: Current flow: provisional allocated on start-of-stream; reserved until final ack or explicit release. If resume sends a new start and final ack happens on a different host, without carryover of provisional ID we might record both allocations as confirmed.

jen: Console idea: surface "provisional vs confirmed" in request detail waterfall and annotate when they came from different routes. Support needs that to quickly see if it's a double-bill or legitimate extra work.

sam: I'll instrument the router to emit header x-resume-session and propagate it across fallback. Also add telemetry fields: provisional_id, provisional_route, resumed_from_session, toolcall_truncated boolean. ETA few hours.

alex: Ops-bot created INF-3130 for this.

ops-bot: Incident INF-3130: "resume+truncate potential double billing" assigned eng-platform.

maria: For analytics: add event join keys on ledger rows: provisional_id (nullable), confirmed_id, provisional_tokens, confirmed_tokens, provisional_route, confirmed_route, toolcall_truncated. That will let SQL detect overlaps in the pipeline.

danny: Reconcile rule draft: if provisional_id is null but there exists a provisional allocation with same session and time window on different route, and confirmed_tokens >= provisional_tokens * 2, flag for manual review. We need a conservative holdback window to avoid false refunds.

jen: UX note: make flagged items visible in console billing view with a small "investigate" banner linking to raw ledger join results. Also expose an admin action to mark a case disputed/refunded.

sam: Reprobed locally: triggered resume to another shard, forced a truncation, ledger shows provisional allocated on original host and a confirmed charge after resume; provisional wasn't released. Uploading trace trace_20260302_local_11.

maria: Mitigation options: 1) quick: in billing pipeline, dedupe confirmed vs provisional by resume_session_id for a 60s window and mark probable duplicates for manual review; 2) longer: ensure router carries provisional_id so resumed host can claim/clear it.

danny: I favor both: short-term analytics reconcile + longer-term protocol change to carry provisional_id. Will draft RFC for router header semantics and required idempotency knobs in ledger.

jen: For console rollout, we should feature-flag the provisional row behind an enable_provisional_view flag to avoid clutter until QA finishes.

alex: Action list: sam - add headers + telemetry; jen - add provisional row UI behind flag; danny - write reconcile playbook & RFC; maria - add analytic fields and run queries once telemetry lands.

ops-bot: Linked INF-3130 to billing team (cc: finance-support).

sam: Quick gotcha: when toolcall truncation returns a partial final ack our runtime currently emits confirmed_tokens from the truncated payload; need to ensure we tag toolcall_truncated and keep pre-trunc provisional context. I'll push a runtime change as well.

maria: If we see many cases in the next 24h, finance may want to auto-suspend charges pending investigation for affected customers. We'll coordinate with support.

danny: I'll include unit tests for resume on different shards and ensure ledger idempotency/claim semantics keep provisional_id unique and transferable.

jen: Thanks all. Once telemetry is in, I'll wire up a console query that shows per-request provisional vs confirmed timeline and route delta. That should speed up support responses.

alex: Great. Please post the trace and sample query results here when ready.
